fact: The article says the Chinese Meteorological Administration supplied Djibouti an AI early-warning system, put in service in December 2025, and handed over MAZU-Djibouti 2.0 on 17 July 2026 to the authorities, with forecasts at 3 km resolution and a three-day horizon, updated every six hours.
The Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority says DPCR Vision AI, launched in 2024, uses cameras and AI to detect potholes and cracks along regional transport corridors and locate them.
DPCR says its CorridorVision AI, which detects road defects in vehicle video, is in deployment and calibration and has covered over 844 km on its 642 km corridor network.
DPCR says CorridorVision AI has identified 2,174 detections across four defect types in its first processing.
